title: 1 Corinthians 6:1-11: forgiving instead of suing
opening_question: Paul asks how a believer can take a brother to law before the unjust. What did Paul say, what did Yeshua say about the one who sues you, how often are we to forgive, and what does it ask of us? Christians read the limits of this teaching differently, and each reading is shown with its own verses.

steps.intro: This path follows the passage of the Sunday message at Crosspoint on 22 November 2026.
steps.question: What did Paul ask about a believer who goes to law against another believer? Before whom did he say they should not go, and who does he say will judge the world?
steps.apply: Do I take my quarrels to people who know Yeshua first?

facts.text: Paul asks whether any of them, having a matter against another, dares to go to law before the unjust and not before the saints.
The saints shall judge the world, and Paul says we shall judge angels, so the smallest matters of this life should not be beyond them.
Daniel 7 says judgment was given to the saints of the most High, that the saints possessed the kingdom, and that the kingdom and dominion will be given to the people of the saints of the most High.

steps.question: What did Yeshua tell His disciples to do when a brother sins against them? Who comes first, who comes second, and who comes last?
steps.apply: Whom have I gone to first?

facts.text: The first step is between the two alone: go and tell him his fault between thee and him alone.
The second step is one or two more, so that every word may be established by two or three witnesses.
The third step is to tell it unto the church.

steps.question: What does Paul say is better than going to law with a brother? Compare what Yeshua said about someone who would sue you and take your coat.
steps.apply: What would I rather lose than keep fighting over?

facts.text: Paul says it is a fault among them to go to law one with another, and asks why they do not rather take wrong.
Yeshua says if any man will sue thee at the law and take away thy coat, let him have thy cloke also.
Yeshua first quotes what had been said, An eye for an eye, and then says But I say unto you.

steps.question: How many times did Peter think was enough to forgive, and what did Yeshua answer? Why does Paul say to forgive, and what does Yeshua say about the one who does not forgive?
steps.apply: Is there someone I still have not forgiven?

facts.text: Peter asks if till seven times is enough. Yeshua answers Until seventy times seven.
Paul gives the reason: forgive even as Christ forgave you.
Yeshua says that if ye forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you, and the reverse.

steps.question: What do Paul, Peter and Proverbs say about paying back evil? What are we told to do instead, and who will repay?
steps.apply: What good can I do to someone who wronged me?

facts.text: Paul says Recompense to no man evil for evil, and avenge not yourselves, for it is written, Vengeance is mine.
Be not overcome of evil, but overcome evil with good.
Peter says Christ, when he was reviled, reviled not again, and committed himself to him that judgeth righteously.

steps.question: What does Paul say about who will not inherit the kingdom of God, and what does he say about the believers in Corinth? Why does Paul remind them of what they were?
steps.apply: What has God already forgiven me?

facts.text: Paul lists the unrighteous who shall not inherit the kingdom of God, then says And such were some of you.
But they are washed, sanctified and justified in the name of the Lord Jesus and by the Spirit of our God.
Titus says we ourselves were once foolish and disobedient, and that He saved us according to his mercy, not by works of righteousness.

steps.question: Christians read this teaching differently: does it forbid every lawsuit, or only a lawsuit between believers before unbelievers? Paul also used Roman law, and Paul wrote that rulers bear the sword. What do the verses say, and what do they not say?
steps.apply: What do these verses say, and what is mine to decide?

facts.text: In 1 Corinthians 6 the matter is believer against believer, and it is taken before the unjust and before the unbelievers.
Paul said I appeal unto Caesar, and he asked the centurion whether it was lawful to scourge a man that is a Roman and uncondemned.
Paul wrote that the ruler beareth not the sword in vain and is a minister of God to thee for good.

remember.text: Paul asks whether any of them dares to go to law before the unjust and not before the saints.
Yeshua said, Until seventy times seven.
Be not overcome of evil, but overcome evil with good.
And such were some of you: but ye are washed, but ye are sanctified, but ye are justified.

quiz.q: Before whom does Paul say a believer should not go to law against another believer?
What does Paul say the saints shall judge?
What does Paul say we shall judge, according to 1 Corinthians 6:3?
What does Paul ask the Corinthians to rather do than go to law?
What does Yeshua say to do if a man will sue you at the law and take away your coat?
options: Let him have your cloke also

quiz.q: How many times did Yeshua say to forgive?
In Matthew 18, who is told the fault first?
options: The brother, between you and him alone

quiz.q: What does Paul say to do to your enemy if he hunger?
What does Paul say overcomes evil?
Whose name and Spirit washed, sanctified and justified the Corinthians?
options: The Lord Jesus and the Spirit of our God

quiz.q: What did Paul say when he stood at Caesar's judgment seat?
